source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/screens/15-settings.png (artboard image is the authority per SETUP); dc.html id="p15"; README screen 15
notes: Region-composition check for the full page: AppShell + the real SettingsPage (its own internal Masthead), populated fixture data via .discipline/rendering/audit/mounts.mjs['compose-settings'] — no live Supabase project reachable in this sandbox (DEVIATION-LOG.md).

Artboard order (dc.html p15): Masthead (VOL line · SETTINGS · scope line ending 'scoped to Dietl / Rockit' · command bar 420px on the SAME row) -> the 'Applies workspace-wide' notice inside the masthead card -> merged 8-entry Account tab row -> R9's S1..S6 section index -> a TWO-COLUMN grid `minmax(0,1fr) 300px`, gap 28: left column (gap 18) Dashboard defaults · Freight sectors · Notifications; right column (gap 14) Briefing schedule · Appearance · Data & supersessions.

SUPERSEDES this spec's train-59 note, which asserted that ruling R9 retires the artboard's 300px rail and that the whole page is one column. R9 retires the second-level SUB-NAV only; the coordinator's train-60 dispatch is explicit that artboard 15 is two columns and that the six designed cards compose into them in the artboard's order. R9's section index stays, and Saved searches / Data summary / CSV upload / Supersession history / Archive / Help stay as anchored sections BELOW the two designed columns (ruling R7: features the artboards draw no region for are kept and listed, placed after the last designed region of the column).

Data-driven differences from the artboard, all logged in DEVIATION-LOG.md 2026-09-08 (lane settings60) and none asserted here as a match: 'Show all 40 sectors' (ALL_SECTORS has 40; the artboard's 36 is its mock corpus), no PDF export segment (`exportFormat` has no `pdf` value and no PDF export path exists), Day segments Mon..Fri (`briefingDay`'s stored union has no Sunday), a Biweekly cadence segment the artboard does not draw (R7), 'Data summary' in place of the rail's 'Export my data' (no data-export path exists anywhere in the app), and the jurisdiction-weighting control kept as a card-foot disclosure rather than the artboard's 'lives in Account -> Jurisdictions' line, which points at a control that does not exist there.

Three shared parts changed for this page, each additively or to the artboards' own value: `AccountCard` gained optional `bodyPadding`/`foot` and lost the tinted plate behind its head (dc.html p14 AND p15 both draw that head on the card's white); `AccountPrimitives` gained `SegmentedControl` (the form dc.html p15 uses five times); `Masthead`'s title/command-bar row became the grid dc.html declares on 15 of the 17 artboards (`minmax(0,1fr) 420px`) instead of a wrapping flex row, which had been pushing the command bar onto its own line whenever the dek was long.

boundsCheck.name: Dashboard defaults control cells — no segmented group escapes its column or overlaps a sibling (operator report 2026-09-07)
boundsCheck.reason: Operator, 2026-09-07: 'your text is too right and it overlays different areas ... the row grid must fit the card width without any cell overflowing its column.' Measured on this page before the fix: at dc.html's literal `6px 12px` segment padding the Alert bands group ran 10px past its own third of the card and the word 'Monitor' was clipped by the card's right edge, because the built content column is 764px where the artboard's is 780. The segment padding is 10px and the grid columns are `minmax(0,1fr)`, and this check measures it from now on rather than trusting the reading.

boundsCheck.reason: The left column's three cards must stay inside the 1fr track and never reach under the 300px rail.
